description:
Hi! I'm a technology professional from Peru with experience in QA, test automation, and web development. I'm passionate about AI, data, and innovative technology solutions.

For the Field Shift challenge, I want to explore how NASA satellite data can help improve potato farming and support agricultural communities in Peru.

I'm looking for teammates with skills in Python, data science, GIS, remote sensing, agronomy, and machine learning.

I developed Qullqa, a free, mobile-first web app that helps Andean smallholder farmers decide what to plant, when to plant it, and what to plant next. For centuries, Andean farmers watched the Pleiades (Qullqa in Quechua) to time their sowing; Qullqa joins that ancestral wisdom with NASA data.

To address the Field Shift challenge, Qullqa adjusts NASA POWER climate data to each farm's real altitude and compares it with crop needs. It shows which crops can grow on the farm and which cannot (and why: altitude, cold, frost or water), the best sowing months, frost and rain risks, and El Niño alerts. Its rotation planner reads the farm's planting and harvest history, tells which crops must rest to protect the soil, and builds a three-season plan that farmers can save, share on WhatsApp and track.

This matters because climate change is shifting rains and frosts in the Andes, while most farmers lack data adapted to their altitude. Qullqa turns satellite data into simple, local decisions that reduce losses and protect food security.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Qullqa is a free, mobile-first web app that helps Andean smallholder farmers decide what to plant, when to plant it, and what to plant next. It joins the Inca tradition of reading the Pleiades (Qullqa in Quechua) to time the sowing season with NASA data:

- Where can I plant? Using the farm's altitude and NASA climate, it lists which crops can grow there, which need care, and which cannot, explaining why (altitude, cold, frost or water). Farmers can add their own crops.

- When to plant: a sowing calendar with frost and rain risks, plus El Niño alerts.

- Crop rotation planner: it reads the farm's planting and harvest history, tells which crops must rest to avoid pests and soil exhaustion (for example, potato waits until 2028), ranks the best next crops for the local climate and builds a three-season plan.

- Save and act: the plan is saved, shared on WhatsApp and shown on the home screen with a countdown to the next sowing. Marking "I planted" updates the history.

- Also: planting and harvest history with yields, a map of Peru's agricultural zones, and a Mars greenhouse simulation.

HOW IT WORKS

NASA POWER monthly climatology (2001-2025) is downloaded for the farm's coordinates and adjusted to its real altitude using the atmospheric lapse rate (6.5 °C per km). Each crop's needs (altitude range, minimum temperature, frost sensitivity, cycle length and water) are compared month by month to find good sowing windows. The rotation engine combines rest years per crop family, climate fit and the farm's own history.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Climate change is shifting rains and frosts in the Andes, and most farmers lack data adapted to their altitude. Qullqa turns satellite data into simple local decisions: fewer losses to frost and drought, healthier soil through rotation, and a written plan farmers can share with family and cooperatives.

TOOLS

React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet and Vitest (115 automated tests), deployed on Vercel. It runs in the browser of low-end phones, with no installation, and stores data on the device. Languages: English, Spanish and Quechua (beta).

CREATIVITY

Qullqa connects ancestral Andean astronomy with satellite data: the same question the Incas answered by looking at the Pleiades, "when and what should I plant?", is answered today with NASA data adjusted to each farm.

FACTORS I CONSIDERED

Altitude (the same region can range from 2,500 to 4,000 m), low connectivity and low-end phones, simple language and icons for farmers with little schooling, WhatsApp as the main way to share, local crops such as native potatoes, quinoa, tarwi and broad beans, and respect for traditional knowledge.

Code: https://github.com/juanmanuel1912/qullqa
